Requirements for manifest and package

Requirements: manifest and package

This page lists every requirement id of the form PKG-nnn. The ids cover the manifest, the package format, signing and trust, the registry, install and update, dependency resolution, the distribution commands, administration, publishing and the plugin store. The table is generated by a script from the definitions on the other pages. Do not edit it by hand. Each row gives the id, the statement, the page that defines it and how a test checks it.

Id ranges: 001 to 099 manifest, 100 to 199 package format, 200 to 259 signing and trust, 260 to 305 install and update, 310 to 360 dependency resolution, 361 to 422 registry, 423 to 446 distribution commands, 460 to 489 administration, 490 to 529 publishing, 530 to 559 plugin store, 560 to 589 manifest schema, 650 to 659 package lifecycle additions (signature document, registry signing and dependency cycles).

Count: 477 requirements. Duplicate definitions: 0. Cited without a definition: 0.

Id Statement Page How to test
PKG-001 The manifest MUST be the entry manifest.json at the root of the package, at most 1 MiB, encoded as UTF-8 without a byte order mark and valid under RFC 8259. A source manifest in a project folder has the same form. reference-manifest Assert code manifest.json
PKG-002 The top-level value MUST be an object. A JSON array, string, number, true, false or null is refused. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-003 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.duplicate-key: no object may hold the same member name twice. The check applies at every depth and before any key is interpreted. It stops the validation.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-004 Comments, trailing commas, single-quoted strings and unquoted keys are not JSON and MUST be refused. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-005 Every key MUST be one the schema defines for that object. An unknown key is refused at every depth. The only objects that accept other names are the JSON Schema subsets (arguments_schema, entry_schema, payload_schema, reply_schema, settings_schema) and the entry object of an extension, w reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-006 null is not a value. A key that is not needed MUST be omitted. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-007 A number that must be an integer MUST be written without a fraction or an exponent (10, not 10.0 or 1e1) and MUST be inside the range of its key. Numbers that are not integers are used only where a key says number. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-008 Nesting MUST NOT be deeper than 32 levels. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-009 Display text (name, publisher, description, titles, labels) MUST NOT contain control characters, line or paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029) or bidirectional override and isolate characters (U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069). reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-010 The order of keys does not change the meaning. ilium plugin pack writes them in the order of the table below and files last. The signature covers the exact bytes of the packed file, so the order after packing MUST NOT be changed. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-011 A source manifest MAY omit files. A packed manifest MUST contain it. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-012 A manifest MUST declare at least one of server, client and scene. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-013 api MUST be the string ilium:plugin@0.1.0. A well-formed ilium:plugin@X.Y.Z outside the window of the host is refused at stage 3 as unsupported. Any other string is a schema error. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-014 id MUST have 2 to 8 segments joined by .. A segment has 1 to 32 characters from a-z, 0-9 and -, and does not start or end with -. The whole id has at most 128 characters. The prefix ilium. is reserved for the release, and core, local and test are reserved as first segments (PKG-2 reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-015 name is the title that the review dialog, the store and the Plugins screen show. It MUST follow PKG-009. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-016 version MUST be a SemVer 2.0.0 string with three numeric parts and an optional prerelease and build part. A leading v is refused. Details: Versions and dependencies. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-017 publisher is a display name. It MUST equal the display name stored with the signing key (PKG-219) for a signed package. It is not an identity. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-018 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.display-name: description is one paragraph shown in the review dialog and the store.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-019 The installer MUST refuse with manifest.schema a license longer than 128 characters or empty (reference-manifest-schema). license is shown and stored; the host checks only the length. A registry publish may require a known SPDX expression.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-020 The client SHOULD draw an icon name that it does not know as the default plugin icon. check reports a warning and the installer never refuses the package for it.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-021 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.schema, registry.category-unknown: categories is required to publish to a registry. A value outside the list is refused at publish.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-022 The installer MUST refuse with manifest.schema a keywords list of more than 8 items, or an item shorter than 1 or longer than 24 characters. keywords feed search only.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-023 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.schema: homepage and repository are shown as text and as a link that the user opens on purpose. The host never fetches them.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-024 A side that is declared MUST have its component in the package (PKG-125). reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-025 capabilities MAY have the keys server, client and scene only. A list for a side without a component is refused. Each list holds at most 256 distinct grants. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-026 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.schema: activation entries follow Activation triggers.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-027 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.requires-invalid, manifest.requires-self: requires is defined in one place only: Versions and dependencies.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-028 Each entry of replaces MUST be a core plugin id. The rules are under Replacement. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-029 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.limits-tier, manifest.schema: replaceable and surface are for core plugins. A third-party package that sets replaceable is refused. surface entries are kind:name with kind one of services, points, commands, pane-kinds, topics and cli.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-030 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.unknown-key: contributes accepts only the keys of the tables below.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-031 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.unknown-key: limits accepts only the keys of the Limits object. A request above the ceiling is clamped, never refused.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-032 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.data-version: data_version is the version of the data layout the plugin writes. A stored version above the manifest value follows the downgrade rule of the data migration guide. Absent means 1. 0 and negative values are refused (rule LIF-100).. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-033 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.limits-tier: limits_tier: "first-party" raises the settings caps for bundled T1 plugins with an ilium. id. Any other package that sets it is refused at stage 9.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-034 An unstable name MUST be a feature of this host. A T2 or T3 package can list one only in development mode. A component that imports an unstable item not named here is refused. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-035 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.files-order, manifest.file-*: files lists every entry except manifest.json and signature, sorted in archive order, with no path twice.. reference-manifest Assert code manifest.json
PKG-040 entry MUST be server.wasm for server, client.wasm for client and scene.wasm for scene. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-041 world MUST be ilium:server/base@0.1.0 for server, ilium:client/base@0.1.0 for client and ilium:anim/base@0.1.0 for scene. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-042 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.schema: [ABI-018] exports lists only the optional exports of that side, once each, from the table below. The required exports (lifecycle and handler, and renderer for a scene) are never listed. Default: the empty list.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-043 The list MUST equal the optional exports that the component really has. Both a missing and an extra name are refused. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-044 A side that lists hook-handler MUST have at least one extension with a handler on that side. A side with such extensions MUST list it. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-045 The following MUST hold. A manifest with data_version above 1 MUST list migrator in exports for each of its server and client components (a scene component has no migrator), and each of those components MUST export it. A component with nothing to migrate exports a migrator that returns ok. Checked at stage 6 with manifest.exports-mismatch (rule LIF-278). reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-050 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.grant-unknown, manifest.grant-argument: a grant is a string of 3 to 256 characters: a name of lower-case words joined by . or -, optionally followed by : and an argument. The first colon separates them.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-051 A grant MUST be a grant of this API version, in the Capability table. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-052 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.grant-argument-missing, manifest.grant-argument: a grant that needs an argument and has none is refused. A grant that takes no argument and has one is refused.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-053 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.grant-wildcard: a wildcard is allowed only where the grant's grammar says so.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-054 A grant MUST be available on the side that lists it. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-055 A grant that needs another grant (fs.pick needs fs.read:picked or fs.write:picked) MUST find it in the same side list. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-056 An fs.* scope MUST be known and accept the access. A process.run argument MUST be a program name or an absolute path, without arguments. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-057 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.grant-tier: a grant for bundled plugins only (high-risk settings.read-all, sessions.cross for T3) is refused for any other tier. The tier is known only after the signature, so this check runs at stage 9.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-058 When declining a grant at install never fails the install. Each import that needs a declined grant returns not-permitted., the client MUST do this: none reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-059 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.schema: activation is a list of at most 32 distinct triggers. Each is startup, durable-timer, or a kind from the table followed by : and a name without spaces. An unknown kind is refused. Without activation, the plugin is lazy.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-060 A trigger that names an own contribution (command:, view:, pane-kind:, scene:, cli:, settings:, catalog:, menu:, virtual-rows:) MUST name one that exists in contributes. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-061 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.contribution-limit, manifest.schema: each list under contributes is an array with at most the number of entries in its cap (32 where the table gives none). An entry id is 1 to 64 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, unique inside its list.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-062 A reference to another contribution (command, popup_view, slot, parent, help) MUST name an entry of this plugin that exists, unless the field says that another plugin's id is allowed. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-063 A file named by help or sounds MUST exist in the package under help/ or sounds/ and be listed in files. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-064 contributes.scenes MUST NOT be present unless the manifest declares a scene component. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-065 A cli name, a sound id and a commands global id MUST NOT collide with another entry of the same plugin. A collision with another installed plugin is found when the second one is installed. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-070 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.schema: every limits value is an integer from 0 to 4,294,967,295 in the unit of its key.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-071 When a value above the ceiling of the tier is clamped to the ceiling and logged. It is never refused. A value of 0 means the default., the client MUST do this: none reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-072 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.unknown-key: a key outside the table is refused.. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-073 When the ceiling comes from the tier, which is known only after the signature check. The manifest cannot raise it., the client MUST do this: none reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-074 The user MAY set the same keys under [plugins.limits] or [plugins."<id>".limits]. The effective value MUST be min(ceiling, v), where v is the first set of the [plugins."<id>".limits] value, the [plugins.limits] value, the manifest value and the default, in that order; 0 or a missing value means not set. The user can raise a value up to the ceiling and can lower it (LIF-143). reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-075 A stage that collects errors MUST report every error it finds in byte order of the JSON pointer of the manifest location it concerns (PKG-578), up to 100. A test with two defects in one stage expects both codes. A test with defects in two stages expects only the earlier one. reference-manifest Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-076 The following MUST hold. Every error carries a code, a message from the template of the catalogue, and, when the error has a place in the document, a pointer (RFC 6901) or a path to it. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-077 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin check on a source manifest runs stages 2 to 4. It reports the same codes and pointers as the installer. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-078 The following MUST hold. The code of every error is in the error catalogue. The older spellings are in the table of retired codes. reference-manifest Review against the page text
[PKG-079] The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.service-name, manifest.file-missing: a provider name whose prefix is neither this plugin's id nor the id of a core plugin in this package's replaces list (accepted only for items in that core plugin's surface), a duplicate name or a missing schema file is refused. reference-manifest Review against the page text
PKG-100 Every entry MUST use compression method 0 (stored). Any other method is refused with package.zip-compressed. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-compressed
PKG-101 General-purpose flag bit 11 (UTF-8 names) MUST be set on every entry. Bit 0 (encryption) and bit 3 (data descriptor) MUST NOT be set. They are refused with package.zip-encrypted and package.zip-descriptor. All other flag bits MUST be zero. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-encrypted, package.zip-descriptor
PKG-102 The archive MUST NOT use ZIP64. A ZIP64 end record, a ZIP64 locator or a size field of 0xFFFFFFFF is refused with package.zip64. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip64
PKG-103 Local headers and central directory headers MUST NOT carry extra fields. The extra field length MUST be 0. Refused with package.zip-extra. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-extra
PKG-104 The end-of-central-directory record MUST have a comment length of 0. No per-entry comment is allowed. Refused with package.zip-comment. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-comment
PKG-105 The archive MUST NOT contain directory entries (names ending in /). Refused with package.entry-directory. reference-package-format Assert code package.entry-directory
PKG-106 The DOS modification time of every entry MUST be 1980-01-01 00:00:00 (time field 0x0000, date field 0x0021). reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-107 The external attributes of every entry MUST be 0x81A40000 (Unix mode 0100644, a regular file with mode 0644). A symbolic link, a device or any other mode is refused with package.entry-symlink. reference-package-format Assert code package.entry-symlink
PKG-108 The "version made by" field MUST be 0x0314 (Unix, specification 2.0) and "version needed to extract" MUST be 20. The disk number fields MUST be 0 and the internal attributes MUST be 0. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-109 For every entry the local header and the central directory header MUST agree on the name, the CRC-32, the compressed size and the uncompressed size. For a stored entry the two sizes are equal. A mismatch is refused with package.header-mismatch. reference-package-format Assert code package.header-mismatch
PKG-110 The CRC-32 of every entry MUST be correct. A wrong CRC is refused with package.crc-mismatch. The host checks it while it reads the entry, before it parses the content. reference-package-format Assert code package.crc-mismatch
PKG-111 The archive MUST consist of the local entries, then the central directory, then the end record, with no other bytes. Bytes before the first local header, between records or after the end record are refused with package.zip-trailing. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-trailing
PKG-112 The local entries MUST be adjacent and in the same order as the central directory, and their byte ranges MUST NOT overlap. A central directory entry whose local header offset does not point to the next unread byte is refused with package.header-mismatch. reference-package-format Assert code package.header-mismatch
PKG-113 The count of entries in the end record MUST equal the count of central directory headers, and the central directory size and offset MUST match the real positions. A truncated or inconsistent central directory is refused with package.zip-invalid. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-invalid
PKG-114 The reader MUST locate the end record by reading the last 22 bytes of the file. Because the comment length is 0, the end record always starts exactly 22 bytes before the end. A file in which that position does not hold the signature PK\x05\x06 is refused with package.zip-invalid. reference-package-format Assert code package.zip-invalid
PKG-115 A path MUST use / as its separator and be made of components of the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, ., _ and - only. Any other byte, including backslash, NUL, a space, a control character or a non-ASCII character, is refused with package.path-invalid. reference-package-format Assert code package.path-invalid
PKG-116 A path MUST NOT start with /, MUST NOT contain an empty component, and MUST NOT contain a component equal to . or ... reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-117 The following MUST hold. No component may start with . or end with .. This keeps hidden files and Windows trailing-dot names out of the package. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-118 A component MUST NOT be a name that Windows reserves (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1 to COM9, LPT1 to LPT9), with or without an extension, in any letter case. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-119 The following MUST hold. A path is at most 255 bytes long and has at most 16 components. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-120 The following MUST hold. No two paths may be equal, and no two paths may be equal after ASCII case folding. A duplicate is refused with package.path-duplicate. A case-only collision is refused with package.path-case-collision, so that the package unpacks the same way on a case-insensitive file system. reference-package-format Assert code package.path-duplicate, package.path-case-collision
PKG-121 The following MUST hold. A path that is a prefix of another path followed by / (a file that is also a folder) is refused with package.path-invalid. reference-package-format Assert code package.path-invalid
PKG-122 Entries MUST be ordered by the bytewise comparison of their UTF-8 paths, which for this character set is ASCII order. Z sorts before a, and / (0x2F) sorts before digits. Out-of-order entries are refused with package.entry-order. reference-package-format Assert code package.entry-order
PKG-123 The following MUST hold. Any top-level entry that is not in the table, and any entry under a top-level folder that the table does not list, is refused with package.entry-unexpected. reference-package-format Assert code package.entry-unexpected
PKG-124 help/ MUST hold only files whose names end in .md. sounds/ MUST hold only .wav and .ogg files. screenshots/ MUST hold only .png files. These folders are flat: a nested folder is refused with package.entry-unexpected. reference-package-format Assert code package.entry-unexpected
PKG-125 A component MUST be named after its side. A file named server.wasm that is declared as the client entry is refused with manifest.entry-invalid. reference-package-format Assert code manifest.entry-invalid
PKG-126 Entries in the archive MUST NOT exceed 4,096. A larger value is refused with package.entry-limit. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-127 manifest.json MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes). A larger value is refused with package.manifest-size. reference-package-format Assert code manifest.json
PKG-128 One component MUST NOT exceed 64 MiB. A larger value is refused with package.size-limit. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-129 One non-component entry MUST NOT exceed 64 MiB. A larger value is refused with package.size-limit. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-130 The package file MUST NOT exceed 300 MiB. A larger value is refused with package.size-limit. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-131 signature MUST NOT exceed 16 KiB. A larger value is refused with package.size-limit. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-132 Asset bytes (assets/**, help/*.md, sounds/*, fonts) MUST NOT exceed 64 MiB, or 256 MiB for T1 (decision D24). A larger value is refused with manifest.asset-size. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-133 The following MUST hold. Each files item has exactly the keys path, length and sha256. path is an archive path. length is the size in bytes of the uncompressed data and is an integer from 0 to 67,108,864 for a non-component entry (PKG-129, refused with package.size-limit), and from 0 to 268,435,456 for an asset entry of a T1 package (PKG-132, refused with manifest.asset-size). sha256 is 64 characters of lowercase hexadecimal. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-134 files MUST list the paths in the same order as the archive (the bytewise order of [PKG-122]), and MUST NOT contain a path twice. A packed manifest whose list is unsorted is refused with manifest.files-order. reference-package-format Assert code manifest.files-order
PKG-135 Every archive entry except manifest.json and signature MUST be in files (manifest.file-unlisted). Every files item MUST name an archive entry (manifest.file-missing). files MUST NOT list manifest.json or signature (manifest.file-self). reference-package-format Assert code manifest.json, manifest.file-unlisted, manifest.file-missing, manifest.file-self
PKG-136 The length of each entry MUST equal length (manifest.file-length), and its SHA-256 MUST equal sha256 (manifest.file-hash). reference-package-format Assert code manifest.file-length, manifest.file-hash
PKG-137 A packed manifest MUST contain files. A source manifest MAY omit it, and ilium plugin pack then writes it. The installer refuses a manifest without files with manifest.key-missing (pointer /files). reference-package-format Assert code manifest.key-missing
PKG-138 A component MUST contain exactly one custom section named ilium:api-version. None gives package.api-section-missing. A second one gives package.api-section-repeated. reference-package-format Assert code package.api-section-missing, package.api-section-repeated
PKG-139 The following MUST hold. The payload (after the section name) is exactly 6 bytes: three unsigned 16-bit integers in big-endian order, for major, minor and patch. For ilium:plugin@0.1.0 the bytes are 00 00 00 01 00 00. Another length gives package.api-section-invalid. reference-package-format Assert code package.api-section-invalid
PKG-140 The three integers MUST equal the version in the manifest api key, or the install is refused with manifest.api-version. reference-package-format Assert code manifest.api-version
PKG-141 The following MUST hold. A file named *.wasm that is a WebAssembly core module, and not a component, is refused with package.component-invalid. The check reads the 8-byte preamble: the magic 00 61 73 6D, then the layer field. Layer 0 is a core module. Layer 1 is a component. reference-package-format Assert code package.component-invalid
PKG-142 The component MUST validate as a component against the world named in the manifest. A component that fails validation is refused with package.component-invalid. A component that exports something that the manifest does not list, or the reverse, is refused with manifest.exports-mismatch. reference-package-format Assert code package.component-invalid, manifest.exports-mismatch
PKG-143 The following MUST hold. Input set. pack includes: the source manifest.json; the built components server.wasm, client.wasm and scene.wasm for each declared side, taken from the build output folder; every file under assets/, help/, sounds/, screenshots/ and src/; and README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE reference-package-format Assert code manifest.json
PKG-144 The following MUST hold. Ignore rules. Inside the included folders pack skips files whose name starts with ., *~, *.swp, *.tmp, and the folders .git, target, node_modules and dist. A skipped file is reported as a warning line. A file that remains and breaks a path rule of this page stops pack with the reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-145 The following MUST hold. Manifest serialisation: UTF-8, 2-space indent, LF and one final LF; top-level keys in table order and files last; nested keys in schema order and unknown maps in byte order; [] and {} on the key line; only ", \ and U+0000 to U+001F escaped; integers only. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-146 The following MUST hold. Archive order and fields. Entries are written in the order of [PKG-122] with the header values of [PKG-100] to [PKG-108]. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-147 Determinism. Two runs of pack over identical inputs MUST give byte-identical files. The test is to compare the SHA-256 of two outputs. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-148 The following MUST hold. Signing. ilium plugin sign adds the signature entry by writing a new archive: it reads the package, adds the entry in its sorted position (it sorts between server.wasm and sounds/, as byte order requires) and rewrites the central directory. Unsigned entries keep their bytes. The result is ag reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-149 The installer MUST run the stages in the order of the table. A stage MUST NOT run when an earlier stage reported an error. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-150 Within a stage that collects errors, the installer MUST report every error it finds, up to 100 per stage. The 101st is replaced by one warning line that says how many more exist. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-151 No plugin code MUST run before stage 11 has finished. Components are not instantiated, and no import is called. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-152 Tier-dependent rules (T1-only grants, limits_tier) run in stage 9, after the tier is known from stages 7 and 8. A source of tier that the user cannot influence MUST NOT be read from the manifest. reference-package-format Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-153 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin check runs stages 2 to 4 on a source manifest (it needs no archive) and, with --package <file>, all stages up to 6. It never contacts the network and never writes state. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-154 The following MUST hold. verify prints one progress line per stage with stage (1 to 7) and name, then one error line per error, then one result line. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-155 The following MUST hold. The result line has ok (boolean), id, version, sha256 (of the package file), manifest_sha256, tier (T2, T3 or untrusted), signer_key_id (or null) and publisher_id (or null). reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-156 The following MUST hold. verify runs stages 1 to 7 (the gating stages; stage 8, trust, is non-gating and only supplies the reported tier) and exits 0 when stages 1 to 7 pass and 1 when any fails. An unknown key prints trust.key-unknown as a warning and reports tier untrusted (exit 0). A revoked key prints trust.key-revoked as an error and exits 1. During install, an unknown key without a prompt answer is an error and exits 1. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-157 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.path-invalid: an entry named ../evil.wasm (zip slip). reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-158 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.path-invalid: an entry named /etc/passwd. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-159 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.path-invalid: an entry named assets\x.png (backslash). reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-160 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.path-invalid: an entry name that holds a NUL byte. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-161 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.entry-unexpected (for Server.wasm) and then package.path-case-collision (for server.wasm): two entries Server.wasm and server.wasm. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-162 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.path-duplicate: two entries with the same name. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-163 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.header-mismatch: a central header whose local offset points into another entry (overlap). reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-164 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.crc-mismatch: one data byte changed, CRC unchanged. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-165 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.zip-invalid: the central directory cut in half. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-166 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.json-invalid: manifest.json with 0 bytes. reference-package-format Assert code manifest.json
PKG-167 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.manifest-missing: an archive with no manifest.json. reference-package-format Assert code manifest.json
PKG-168 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.zip-compressed: one entry stored with method 8 (deflate). reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-169 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.zip-encrypted: bit 0 set on one entry. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-170 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.zip-comment: an archive comment of 4 bytes. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-171 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.zip-trailing: 16 bytes appended after the end record. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-172 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.entry-symlink: a symbolic link entry (mode 0120777). reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-173 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.entry-directory: a directory entry assets/. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-174 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.entry-unexpected: an unlisted file extra.txt at the top level. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-175 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.entry-order: the entries manifest.json and server.wasm swapped. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-176 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.entry-limit: an archive with 4,097 entries. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-177 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.component-invalid: server.wasm replaced by a core module (layer 0). Rebuild with pack after the change, so files lists the new length and SHA-256 and the CRC-32 is correct. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-178 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.api-section-repeated: the api-version section duplicated. Rebuild with pack after the change, so files lists the new length and SHA-256 and the CRC-32 is correct. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-179 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.api-section-invalid: the api-version payload 5 bytes long. Rebuild with pack after the change, so files lists the new length and SHA-256 and the CRC-32 is correct. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-180 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.api-version: the api-version payload 00 00 00 02 00 00. Rebuild with pack after the change, so files lists the new length and SHA-256 and the CRC-32 is correct. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-181 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.file-hash: one byte of server.wasm changed, with a matching CRC. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-182 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.signature-invalid: a signed package with the letter M of the manifest name changed to N, and the correct CRC-32 written to both headers, so that only stage 7 fails. reference-package-format Review against the page text
PKG-200 A signature MUST be an Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032, "pure" Ed25519) over the message M below. Ed25519ph and Ed25519ctx MUST NOT be used. reference-signing-and-trust Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-201 The following MUST hold. M is the concatenation of: the 25 ASCII bytes ilium-plugin-signature-v1, one 0x00 byte, the UTF-8 bytes of the publisher id, one 0x00 byte, and the 32 raw bytes of the SHA-256 of manifest.json. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.json
PKG-202 The SHA-256 is computed over the exact bytes of the manifest.json entry as stored in the archive. The host MUST NOT parse, normalise or re-serialise the manifest before hashing. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.json
PKG-203 A verifier MUST reject a signature when the public key is not a valid Ed25519 point or when the signature is not canonical (S not smaller than the group order). RFC 8032 section 5.1.7 rules apply. reference-signing-and-trust Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-204 The document MUST have exactly the keys format and signatures. format MUST be ilium-sig/1. reference-signing-and-trust Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-205 signatures MUST hold 1 to 4 objects. Each has exactly the keys algorithm (ed25519), key_id, publisher_id, signature and signed_at. reference-signing-and-trust Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-206 The following MUST hold. key_id is 64 characters of lowercase hexadecimal. signature is the 64 signature bytes in base64url without padding (86 characters). signed_at is YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in UTC and is informational: the host never uses it for a decision. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-207 The first object is the publisher signature. A second object MAY be a registry countersignature (see Registry reference). The host verifies every object and requires at least one valid object from a trusted key. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-208 The following MUST hold. The entry is at most 16 KiB. A document that does not match these rules is refused with package.signature-format. A signature that does not verify is refused with manifest.signature-invalid. A key_id that does not match any key that verifies the signature is manifest.signature-invalid. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code package.signature-format, manifest.signature-invalid
PKG-209 The following MUST hold. The entry sorts like any other entry (bytewise by path). Adding it keeps the archive valid and deterministic ([PKG-148]). reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-650 The following MUST hold. The signature document is serialised with the rules of PKG-145: UTF-8 without a byte order mark, 2-space indentation, LF line endings and one final LF. Keys appear in table order: format, signatures; in each object algorithm, key_id, publisher_id, signature, signed_at. Two runs of sign with the same key, manifest and signed_at MUST give byte-identical packages. reference-signing-and-trust Pack and sign twice with the same inputs and compare the SHA-256 of the two packages
PKG-651 The following MUST hold. signed_at is taken by sign from --signed-at <time> (the form YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss, in UTC), else from the environment variable SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), else from the clock. The test vector below was made with --signed-at "2026-10-12 10:00:00". reference-signing-and-trust Sign with each source of the time and compare the signed_at value
PKG-210 publisher.key MUST be a PKCS#8 (RFC 5958) private key in PEM, with the label PRIVATE KEY, or ENCRYPTED PRIVATE KEY when protected by a passphrase. reference-signing-and-trust Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-211 The following MUST hold. An encrypted key uses PBES2 with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (at least 600,000 iterations) and AES-256-CBC. keygen encrypts when --passphrase-file or the environment variable ILIUM_KEY_PASSPHRASE is given or when the user types a passphrase at the prompt. An empty passphrase is refused. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-212 keygen MUST create the file with mode 0600 and the folder with mode 0700. sign MUST refuse a key file that is readable by group or others (sign.key-permissions), on systems that have such modes. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code sign.key-permissions
PKG-213 sign --key - reads the PEM from standard input. The environment variable ILIUM_PUBLISHER_KEY MAY hold the PEM text for CI use. The host never writes a private key to a log. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-214 public_key is the 32 raw bytes in base64url without padding. key_id MUST equal the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those 32 bytes. A file with another key_id is refused with trust.key-malformed. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.key-malformed
PKG-215 The following MUST hold. publisher_id follows the grammar below. publisher is a display name of 1 to 64 characters with no control and no bidirectional-override characters. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-216 Fingerprint display. The stored form is the 64-character hex string. The display form groups it in 16 groups of 4 characters separated by single spaces, and the dialog splits it into two lines of 8 groups. [PKG-216] A dialog or prompt that asks the user to trust a key MUST show all 64 characters. It reference-signing-and-trust Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-217 The following MUST hold. A publisher id matches [a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*){0,3}, is 1 to 64 characters long and has at most 4 segments. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-218 A signed package's plugin id MUST start with <publisher_id>. where publisher_id is the one in the signature. Otherwise the install is refused with manifest.id-publisher. Example: publisher id com.acme signs com.acme.notes. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.id-publisher
PKG-219 The manifest publisher text MUST equal (after Unicode NFC normalisation, case-sensitive) the display name stored with the key in the trust store. A mismatch is refused with manifest.publisher-mismatch. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.publisher-mismatch
PKG-220 The following MUST hold. The prefix ilium. is reserved for the release. No key can be trusted for the publisher id ilium, core, local or test. Adding such a key is refused with trust.publisher-reserved. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.publisher-reserved
PKG-221 The following MUST hold. The user store is the file trust.json in the Ilium user state folder ($XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/trust.json; ~/.local/state/ilium/trust.json on Linux when XDG_STATE_HOME is unset). It is created with mode 0600. Writes are atomic: write a temporary file in the same folder, fsync, rename. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.json
PKG-222 The following MUST hold. The system store is /etc/ilium/trust.json on Linux (the platform equivalent through the same crate elsewhere). It is read-only for the host. An administrator owns it. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-223 The following MUST hold. The effective trust set is the union of both stores minus every revoked key. A key revoked in either store is revoked. A user cannot remove or override a system entry. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-224 Each store entry binds one key_id to exactly one publisher_id. A second entry with the same key_id and another publisher id is refused with trust.publisher-conflict. One publisher id MAY have several keys (needed for rotation). reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.publisher-conflict
PKG-225 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin install --trust <key_id> trusts that exact key for this install and for later ones. It is the only non-interactive way to trust a key. A package signed by another key is refused with trust.key-unknown. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.key-unknown
PKG-226 The following MUST hold. trust remove of a key that signed installed plugins MUST be refused with trust.in-use and list the plugins, unless --force is given. With --force the plugins enter package state disabled-untrusted; trusting the key again, or enable --accept-risk, leaves it. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.in-use
PKG-227 trust remove MUST NOT delete any plugin data. trust remove of a system entry is refused with trust.system-entry. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.system-entry
PKG-228 The following MUST hold. A package with a valid signature from a trusted, non-revoked key is tier T2. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-229 The following MUST hold. A package with no signature entry is tier T3. It installs only with --allow-unsigned, or through ilium plugin dev. Without either it is refused with install.unsigned. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code install.unsigned
PKG-230 The following MUST hold. A package with a valid signature from a key that is not in the trust store prompts the user with the key details. If the user accepts, the key is added with added_by: user and the install continues as T2. If the user declines, the install stops with trust.declined. In a non-interactive run witho reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.declined, trust.key-unknown
PKG-231 The following MUST hold. A package with an invalid signature is refused with manifest.signature-invalid, whatever the user could choose. There is no flag that installs it. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.signature-invalid
PKG-232 The following MUST hold. A package signed by a revoked key is refused with trust.key-revoked. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.key-revoked
PKG-233 The following MUST hold. T1 is not a trust-store tier. A T1 component is a component embedded in the Ilium release. At build time the release records the SHA-256 of each embedded component in a table inside the binary. At load time the host compares the embedded bytes with the table. A mismatch disables the plugin with `tru reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.bundled-tampered
PKG-234 The following MUST hold. A package from any source whose id starts with ilium. is refused with manifest.id-reserved, even when it carries a valid signature. Core plugins change only with a new Ilium release. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.id-reserved
PKG-235 The following MUST hold. The declared tier never comes from the manifest. There is no manifest key for it. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-236 The following MUST hold. When a plugin is installed and an update is signed by a key with another key_id than the installed version's key, the host checks the trust store. If the new key is already trusted for the same publisher id, the update continues. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-237 Otherwise the update MUST be refused with package.publisher-key-changed, and the message names both fingerprints. No dialog can override this inside install. The user changes the situation first, by importing a rotation statement or by running trust add --additional. This decision keeps a stol reference-signing-and-trust Assert code package.publisher-key-changed
PKG-238 The following MUST hold. A rotation statement is the document rotation.json: { "format": "ilium-rot/1", "publisher_id", "old_key_id", "new_key": { "public_key", "key_id" }, "signature", "created" }. signature is made by the old key over the message ilium-key-rotation-v1, 0x00, the publisher id, 0x00, the 32 raw reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-239 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin trust add --rotation <rotation.json> verifies the statement against the old key in the store. If valid, it adds the new key with added_by: user for the same publisher id, and keeps the old key as trusted until the user or the publisher revokes it. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-240 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin trust add --additional <publisher.pub> adds a second key for a publisher id that already has a key. It shows the old and the new fingerprints and requires typing the word replace in an interactive session. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-241 A rotation statement MUST be signed by a key that is currently trusted for the same publisher id. Otherwise trust.rotation-invalid. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.rotation-invalid
PKG-242 The following MUST hold. A revocation statement is the document { "format": "ilium-rev/1", "publisher_id", "key_id", "reason", "effective", "signature" }. reason is compromised, superseded or retired. effective is YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in UTC. signature is made by the revoked key itself, or by the new key name reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-243 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin trust revoke <key_id> --reason <reason> writes the key as revoked in the user store. A registry (when configured) distributes revocations in its metadata. See Registry reference. The administrator also revokes keys in the system store. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-244 The following MUST hold. New installs of a package signed by a revoked key are refused with trust.key-revoked, for every reason. reference-signing-and-trust Assert code trust.key-revoked
PKG-245 The following MUST hold. Installed plugins signed by a key revoked as compromised are stopped at once and enter package state disabled-blocked. They leave it only with ilium plugin enable <id> --accept-risk or an update signed by another trusted key of the same publisher. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-246 The following MUST hold. Installed plugins signed by a key revoked as superseded or retired keep running at T2 with the badge key retired. Updates must come from a trusted key of the same publisher id. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-247 The following MUST hold. The host checks the revocation lists whenever the trust stores or the registry metadata change, and at every start. A revocation with an effective time in the future applies when that time passes. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-248 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.signature-invalid: one byte of manifest.json changed (and the CRC repaired). reference-signing-and-trust Assert code manifest.json
PKG-249 When one byte of server.wasm changed, manifest unchanged, the client MUST do this: manifest.file-hash (stage 5, before the signature) reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-250 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.signature-invalid: one byte of the signature value changed. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-251 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.signature-invalid: the prefix ilium-plugin-signature-v2 used to sign. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-252 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.signature-invalid: the same key signs with publisher id other but the document says example. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-253 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.id-publisher: the document lists publisher_id: "other" and the plugin id is example.minimal. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-254 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.signature-format: format is ilium-sig/2. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-255 The installer MUST refuse this input with trust.key-unknown: a key not in the trust store, non-interactive, no --trust. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-256 The installer MUST refuse this input with manifest.publisher-mismatch: the key is in the store with display name "Other Labs". reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-257 The installer MUST refuse this input with trust.key-revoked: the key is revoked as compromised. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-258 The installer MUST refuse this input with package.publisher-key-changed: an installed example.minimal signed by key A, an update signed by key B, no rotation. reference-signing-and-trust Review against the page text
PKG-260 The following MUST hold. A URL install downloads the file into the cache folder (<cache dir>/ilium/plugins/downloads/), then treats it as a local file. A URL with the scheme http is refused with install.insecure-url. The download follows at most 3 redirects, all to HTTPS. reference-install-and-update Assert code install.insecure-url
PKG-261 The following MUST hold. The download is at most 300 MiB. A larger response is aborted with install.size. The server's content type is ignored. The file is judged only by the package format. reference-install-and-update Assert code install.size
PKG-262 The following MUST hold. A URL install of an unsigned package needs --allow-unsigned, as a file does. A URL does not change the trust rules. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-263 The following MUST hold. A registry id with a range resolves through Versions and dependencies to one version and then installs that package. The recorded source is registry and the record keeps the registry URL. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-264 A file named in a project recommendation is treated like any other source after the user confirms it. The host MUST NOT download or install a recommended plugin without an explicit user action. reference-install-and-update Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-265 The following MUST hold. Each plugin entry of installed.json follows the one schema of Install, update and uninstall: source is bundled, file, url, registry or dev; channel is stable, beta, dev or file; key_id is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters or null; package_sha256 and manifest_sha256 are 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; skip and declined are lists of version strings; installed_at is RFC 3339 in UTC with the suffix Z; update is null or { candidate, state, attempts, started_at }. The page that owns the schema is the only place that lists the fields. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-266 The following MUST hold. The package file is kept as store/<id>/<version>/package.iliumpkg next to the unpacked files, so that verify and rollback need no network. Files in store/ are written once and made read-only. An update writes a new folder and never changes an old one. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-267 The following MUST hold. The user trust store is $XDG_STATE_HOME/ilium/trust.json (Linux ~/.local/state/ilium/trust.json when XDG_STATE_HOME is unset), mode 0600, written atomically. The variable ILIUM_TRUST_STORE replaces it and holds an absolute file path. The format is that of Signing and trust. Downloads in progress live in <cache dir>/ilium/plugins/downloads/. Cached registry metadata lives in <cache dir>/ilium/plugins/registry/<hash-of-url>/. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-268 The compiled cache <cache dir>/ilium/plugins/compile/ is derived data, keyed by the component SHA-256 and an engine id (the Wasmtime version and settings). The host MUST be able to delete it at any time and recompile. reference-install-and-update Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-269 The following MUST hold. A crash leaves installed.json unchanged, because the registry file is the single commit point (steps 6 below). Orphans in staging/ are deleted at the next start. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-270 The following MUST hold. A second install, update or uninstall that starts while the lock is held polls every 100 ms for up to 30 s and then fails with install.locked, exit code 4 (LIF-066). The lock is an exclusive OS advisory lock, so a crashed holder releases it by process exit and no takeover rule exists. reference-install-and-update Assert code install.locked
PKG-271 The following MUST hold. A crash before step 6 leaves the previous installed.json. The next start deletes the staging/ directories that installed.json does not reference. A crash after step 6 and before step 7 leaves a complete install that the running servers see when they watch installed.json (LIF-089). reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-272 The host MUST NOT instantiate any component before step 6 has finished and step 7 has been sent. reference-install-and-update Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-273 The following MUST hold. The platform gate is stage 9: on Windows and macOS an install of a T2 or T3 package is refused with package.platform-unsupported before the review dialog. T1 bundled plugins are not installed by this path. reference-install-and-update Assert code package.platform-unsupported
PKG-274 The following MUST hold. An install of an id that is already installed at the same version with the same manifest SHA-256 is a no-op: it exits 0 and prints install.already-installed as a warning. With --reinstall it rewrites store/<id>/<version>/ from the package. A different manifest SHA-256 at the same version is refused at stage 9 with package.version-reused, exit 1. The manifest hash is compared, not the package hash, because the signature document changes the package bytes (LIF-072). reference-install-and-update Assert code install.already-installed, package.version-reused
PKG-275 The following MUST hold. --dry-run runs stages 1 to 10 of the validation order without writing anything; stage 11 (the review) is printed as records and never asked, as [PKG-427] says. It prints the plan and exits with the code the real install would give (0 if all stages pass). reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-276 The following MUST hold. The installed set is per user, not per session. Every session of the same user sees the same installed.json. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-277 The following MUST hold. Step 7 sends the message plugins-changed to every server of the user. A server that cannot be reached reads installed.json when it next starts or when its watcher sees the file change. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-278 The following MUST hold. A new plugin is registered and activated by its triggers in each server that gets the notice. An update does not touch running instances: the candidate waits in store/<id>/<version>/ with update.state: staged, and the old version keeps running until it deactivates with reason upgrade, then the candidate activates. The server does this at the next safe point: when the plugin is idle, or at the next server start. The user can force it with ilium plugin restart <id>. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-279 When two sessions run the same plugin, each switches independently. The order across sessions is not defined, and no plugin may rely on two sessions running the same version at one moment. State kept in data/ is shared, so a plugin that changes its data format MUST handle both versions during the reference-install-and-update Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-280 The following MUST hold. Versions compare with the precedence of Versions and dependencies. A prerelease is lower than its release. An equal version is not an update. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-281 The following MUST hold. Grants: new grants (strings that the active version did not request) are asked in the review. Removed grants are dropped from the record. Grants that the user declined before stay declined and are not asked again, unless the new manifest requests them again in a different form (a different argument reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-282 The following MUST hold. A new high-risk grant, a new replaces entry or a new high-risk extension point contribution always needs confirmation. --yes does not confirm it. The flag --grant <grant> for that exact grant does. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-283 The following MUST hold. A publisher key change follows Signing and trust. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-284 The following MUST hold. Settings values, plugin data and storage are kept. The old version deactivates with reason upgrade, which lets it save state, and the new version activates and reads the same data. See Lifecycle. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-285 The following MUST hold. After a successful update the host keeps the previous version folder in store/ and deletes older ones, which matches LIF-076: exactly one previous version stays on disk. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-286 The following MUST hold. The candidate becomes active_version only after its first activate returns ok on the server side. If that first activate fails, traps or misses its deadline, the host rolls back at once to the previous version and its pre-update data snapshot, marks the candidate skip, logs update.rolled-back and does not count the failure in the failure window (LIF-075). Failures after a successful first activation follow the normal failure window and never roll back by themselves. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-287 The following MUST hold. A package whose version is lower than the active version is refused with package.downgrade unless --allow-downgrade is given. reference-install-and-update Assert code package.downgrade
PKG-288 The following MUST hold. A downgrade or rollback to a version whose data_version is lower than the stamp of any bucket in scope is refused with migration.data-newer, exit 1, unless --restore-backup or --discard-data is given (LIF-079). The host never converts newer data downward. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-289 The following MUST hold. A downgrade keeps the replaced newer version as the one previous version on disk, so a later update to it needs no download. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-290 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin rollback <id> makes the one previous version in store/ active. It runs the same transaction as an update, but without the version comparison, and keeps the current grants where the old manifest still asks for them. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-291 The following MUST hold. Rollback is refused with install.no-previous when no earlier version is on disk. reference-install-and-update Assert code install.no-previous
PKG-292 The following MUST hold. After a rollback the rolled-back version is marked skip and is not offered by update until a still newer version exists or the user clears the mark with --unskip. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-293 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin uninstall <id> deactivates the plugin (reason disabled), withdraws all of its contributions, removes the record from installed.json and deletes store/<id>/. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-294 The following MUST hold. Without --purge the folders data/<id>/ and storage/<id>/, the stored settings and backups/<id>/ remain, so a later reinstall finds its configuration. No prompt is shown: the command prints the kept paths as warning lines (LIF-082). Grants, first-use answers, durable timers, failure counters and decorations are deleted on every uninstall (LIF-083), so a reinstall asks for grants again. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-295 The following MUST hold. --purge also deletes data/<id>/, storage/<id>/, backups/<id>/, locks/<id>.*, the plugin log, the stored settings values of the plugin (including project-scoped ones in .ilium/ of the current project only), the plugin cache and the compiled cache entries. It never deletes anything outside these paths. It prints the number of bytes freed. The grant entry is deleted without --purge as well. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-296 The following MUST hold. The trusted key stays in the trust store. Uninstall never edits trust. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-297 The following MUST hold. Dependants follow Versions and dependencies. A plugin installed by a system administrator as read-only is refused with policy.managed-plugin. reference-install-and-update Assert code policy.managed-plugin
PKG-298 The following MUST hold. The uninstall of a plugin that is currently failed or disabled works the same way. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-299 The following MUST hold. A T1 bundled plugin cannot be uninstalled. It can be disabled. The command is refused with install.bundled. reference-install-and-update Assert code install.bundled
PKG-300 The following MUST hold. The setting [plugins] auto_update has the values off (default), notify and install. With off the host never checks the network by itself. With notify it checks and shows a notice. With install it checks and installs updates that need no new grants. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-301 The following MUST hold. The check runs at server start, then every 24 hours while the server runs, with a random delay of up to 1 hour. [plugins] auto_update_interval_hours (1 to 168) changes it. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-302 The following MUST hold. Auto-install never installs an update that adds grants, adds replaces, changes the publisher key, or crosses to a channel the user did not select. Those updates produce a notice and wait. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-303 The following MUST hold. When the network is marked metered (the operating system says so, or [plugins] metered = true), the host does not check. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-304 The following MUST hold. A notice lists the plugin, the old and new version, the new grants and the link to the changelog. The user can Update, Later (which hides the notice for that version for 7 days) or Skip this version. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-305 The following MUST hold. Auto-update is a policy item. An administrator can set off and lock it. reference-install-and-update Review against the page text
PKG-310 The following MUST hold. A version matches MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -prerelease, as SemVer 2.0.0 defines. MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH are integers from 0 to 2,147,483,647 without leading zeros. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-311 The following MUST hold. A prerelease is dot-separated identifiers of [0-9A-Za-z-]. Numeric identifiers have no leading zeros. The whole version is at most 64 characters. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-312 The following MUST hold. A leading v is not part of a version. v1.2.3 is refused with manifest.version-invalid. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code manifest.version-invalid
PKG-313 Authors SHOULD build metadata (+build.5) is allowed in a source manifest. It is ignored in every comparison and two versions that differ only in build metadata are equal. A registry refuses a version that has build metadata (registry.version-invalid), so each registry version has one meaning. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code registry.version-invalid
PKG-314 The following MUST hold. Precedence follows SemVer 2.0.0 section 11. A prerelease is lower than the release with the same numbers: 1.0.0-beta.2 is lower than 1.0.0. Numeric identifiers compare as numbers. Alphanumeric identifiers compare in ASCII order. A numeric identifier is lower than an alphanumeric one. A shorter l reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-315 A range is one or more comparators separated by single spaces. A version satisfies the range when it satisfies all comparators (logical AND). The operator || is not supported and is refused with manifest.requires-invalid. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-316 The following MUST hold. A comparator is one of: an exact version =1.2.3 or 1.2.3, >1.2.3, >=1.2.3, <1.2.3, <=1.2.3, a caret range ^1.2.3, a tilde range ~1.2.3, or the star *. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-317 The following MUST hold. A bare version with no operator (1.2.3, 1.2, 1) means a caret range. This is the Cargo rule. It makes 0.1.0 and ^0.1.0 the same in requires.plugins ranges and point references. It does not apply to requires.services, which takes only a full version (PKG-327). reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-318 The following MUST hold. A caret range ^M.m.p accepts versions that do not change the left-most non-zero part: ^1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 <2.0.0. ^0.2.3 is >=0.2.3 <0.3.0. ^0.0.3 is >=0.0.3 <0.0.4. ^0.0 is >=0.0.0 <0.1.0. ^0 is >=0.0.0 <1.0.0. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-319 The following MUST hold. A tilde range ~M.m.p accepts patch changes: ~1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 <1.3.0. ~1.2 is >=1.2.0 <1.3.0. ~1 is >=1.0.0 <2.0.0. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-320 The following MUST hold. * accepts every release version. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-321 The following MUST hold. A prerelease version satisfies a range only if some comparator of the range has the same MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and itself carries a prerelease (the npm rule), or when the resolver runs on the beta channel for that plugin (see Channels). 1.3.0-beta.1 does not satisfy ^1.2.0 on the stable channel. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-322 The following MUST hold. A range is at most 128 characters. An invalid range is refused with manifest.requires-invalid. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code manifest.requires-invalid
PKG-323 A plugin MUST NOT list its own id in requires.plugins. It is refused with manifest.requires-self. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code manifest.requires-self
PKG-324 requires.plugins MUST NOT name an id twice. Duplicates are refused with manifest.requires-invalid. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code manifest.requires-invalid
PKG-325 The following MUST hold. requires.host is checked against the version of the running Ilium release. A release that does not satisfy it is refused with dependency.host-version at install and keeps the plugin disabled with a reason at load time. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code dependency.host-version
PKG-326 The following MUST hold. wait_ms replaces the fixed 2 s activation wait of the lifecycle page. It is the time a plugin's activation waits for each required service provider. The default is 2000, the range is 0 to 5000, and a value outside the range is refused with manifest.requires-invalid (reference-dependency-resolution). reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-327 The following MUST hold. The service form in requires.services is interface@<major>.<minor>.<patch>, a full version that means the minimum compatible version (the caret range ^<major>.<minor>.<patch>, so ilium:inference/provider@0.1.0 means ^0.1.0). The range grammar of this page does not apply to services: a short form such as @0.1, a caret, a tilde or any range is refused with manifest.service-version (PKG-579). reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-328 The following MUST hold. An extension point reference <plugin-id>/<point>@<minimum> in contributes.extensions.point uses the same grammar: the part after @ is a range, and a bare version is a caret range. requires.points does not exist. The point reference is the dependency. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-329 [PKG-329] Services and points MUST NOT block an install. This keeps the rule of the versioned-service tutorial: a missing provider never makes install fail. Only requires.host, non-optional requires.plugins and a service cycle (PKG-654) block. reference-dependency-resolution Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-330 The following MUST hold. The inputs are: the plugin being installed, the installed plugins with their current versions, the pins (see below), the available sources, and the user's channel settings. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-331 The following MUST hold. For each required plugin id, the resolver collects every range from every installed or incoming plugin that requires it. The chosen version is the highest version that satisfies all ranges, is permitted by the channel and is not yanked. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-332 The following MUST hold. A version that is already installed is preferred over a higher one when it satisfies all ranges and the command is not an update. The resolver does not upgrade a dependency during an install of another plugin unless the range forces it. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-333 The following MUST hold. When no version satisfies all ranges, the resolver refuses with dependency.conflict. The message lists each constraint with its source plugin, and the versions that were available. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code dependency.conflict
PKG-334 The following MUST hold. When a required id has no installed copy and no source has it, the resolver refuses with dependency.unresolved and lists every missing id with its range. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code dependency.unresolved
PKG-335 The following MUST hold. The resolver builds a graph from requires.plugins edges that are not optional. A cycle is refused with dependency.cycle, naming the cycle in order. Cycles through optional edges never block install. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code dependency.cycle
PKG-654 The following MUST hold. A cycle in the graph whose edges are the non-optional requires.services entries, resolved against the installed set plus the package, is refused at stage 10 with manifest.service-cycle, listing the service names in cycle order starting with the smallest. Activation order is therefore always a directed acyclic graph. reference-dependency-resolution Install two plugins whose non-optional service requirements form a cycle and read the code and the order of names
PKG-336 The following MUST hold. The tie-break between equal candidates is the order: highest version, then the source order in the configuration, then the lowest sha256 of the package. The result is deterministic. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-337 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin install --dry-run prints the resolution plan without changing anything. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-338 With installed state (none) and request (A needs B ^1.0, source has B 1.0.0, 1.2.0, 2.0.0), the resolver MUST produce: B 1.2.0 installed, then A reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-339 With installed state (B 1.0.0) and request (A needs B ^1.0), the resolver MUST produce: B 1.0.0 kept. No dependency change reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-340 With installed state (B 1.0.0) and request (A needs B ^1.1, source has B 1.2.0), the resolver MUST produce: B updated to 1.2.0, then A. The user sees both in the review reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-341 Given C needs B ^1.0 and A needs B ^2.0, resolution MUST be refused with dependency.conflict naming C and A. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-342 Given A needs B and no source has B, resolution MUST be refused with dependency.unresolved. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-343 Given A needs B and B needs A (hard), resolution MUST be refused with dependency.cycle. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-344 With installed state (none) and request (A needs B optional, no B), the resolver MUST produce: A installed. B is not required reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-345 With installed state (none) and request (A needs service S, no provider), the resolver MUST produce: A installed. State waiting for S reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-346 Given A needs host >=9.0.0 and the running release is 0.1.0, resolution MUST be refused with dependency.host-version. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-347 Given A needs B ^1.0, only B 1.3.0-beta.1 exists and the channel is stable, resolution MUST be refused with dependency.unresolved. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-348 The following MUST hold. Updating plugin B is refused with dependency.conflict when the new version would leave an installed dependant outside its range. The message offers ilium plugin update --all or update B A to update both together when a satisfying version of A exists. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code dependency.conflict
PKG-349 The following MUST hold. ilium plugin uninstall B is refused with dependency.in-use when an installed, enabled plugin requires B (not optional). --force removes B anyway. The dependants are then disabled with the reason requires B and are re-enabled when B is installed again. reference-dependency-resolution Assert code dependency.in-use
PKG-350 The following MUST hold. The start order is Kahn's algorithm over the edges of the non-optional requires.plugins entries and of the requires.services entries to their providers. At each step the host takes the ready node with the smallest key: the tier number (T1 first), then the plugin id in byte order. Up to 4 activations run at once, started in that order (LIF-045 to LIF-047). reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-351 The following MUST hold. Shutdown runs the exact reverse of the start order, not the reverse of the order in which activations finished. Stops run one at a time (LIF-050). reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-352 A plugin with replaces: ["id"] satisfies a requires.plugins entry for the replaced id when the replacement is enabled and its version satisfies the range. The replacement is a different plugin, so its own version is compared with the range. A consumer that needs the replaced plugin's version series MUST name a range that the replacement also satisfies, or declare the dependency optional. reference-dependency-resolution Conformance test of the stated behaviour
PKG-353 The following MUST hold. Each registry version belongs to exactly one channel. A version with a prerelease part belongs to beta. A version without one belongs to stable or beta, and the publisher chooses at publish time. reference-dependency-resolution Review against the page text
PKG-354 A user sets the default channel in [plugins] channel = "stable" (default stable) and can set a channel for one plugin with ilium plugin channel <id> <stable\|beta>.
